items.title: Fed minutes October 2026: Officials expect more rate hikes, worry about AI
items.excerpt: Key Points - At the Fed's October meeting, almost all participants said that further rate hikes "would likely be appropriate," according to newly released minutes. - AI was a major topic of discussion, and was viewed as a driver of both inflation and potential financial instability. - Officials said they expect inflation to fall off sharply in 2027 and beyond. ... Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk." More broadly, officials said "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting. A couple of participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December. ... Ultimately, the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate locked in a range between 3.75%-4%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. ... Since the meeting, the inflation data has shown that the pace of price increases remains well above target. The consumer price index in October rose 0.4% for all items and 0.3% for the core that excludes food and energy. Both readings were 0.1 percentage point higher than expected.

items.title: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
items.excerpt: Key Points - The Federal Reserve's Christopher Waller said a half percentage point increase in the central bank's benchmark rate is probably necessary at its December meeting. - Alternatively, the Fed could raise rates by a quarter point and signal another move was coming in January, Waller told CNBC, though this runs contrary to how Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has preferred to communicate plans. - Inflation is "headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller told CNBC. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation, saying the central bank needs to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected. In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half percentage point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee. He said the central bank needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more. ... Futures prices are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the FOMC's December meeting. They also are anticipating another move in January, followed by at least one additional increase before the end of 2027, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge.

items.title: Economic commentary: Inflation broadens as AI investment risk rises |
items.excerpt: Inflation readings for September and October were generally stronger than expected. Headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose 0.6% in September, driven in large part by a 9.1% increase in gasoline prices, and that was followed by a stronger than expected 0.4% increase in October, bringing the year-over-year reading to 3.9%. The increases have been broad-based, with no major category registering a decline. Core CPI rose 0.3% in both months. This was the third straight month of a 0.3% reading for core CPI, and the three-month pace at 3.7% annualized is the highest since April 2024. The Producer Price Index (PPI) has also firmed, pushing its year over year increase to the highest level since 2022. Energy prices, particularly diesel, remain the primary driver of producer price pressures. The Fed is concerned that inflation is broadening, and these recent reports do not alleviate that concern.

items.title: Fed’s Barr says rate rises likely lie ahead for economy By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday he’s likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures. “If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further,” Barr said in the text of remarks prepared for delivery before a conference at the New York Fed. “Inflation is too high, making it hard for American families to make ends meet. Many families are struggling” under the weight of price pressures, Barr said. The official also noted that while inflation is an issue, the economy is otherwise doing well. “The economy is strong, with low unemployment, solid consumer spending, and robust business investment,” Barr said. The Fed’s interest-rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on December 8 and 9. It is widely expected to raise its current federal funds target rate range by a quarter percentage point, to between 4% and 4.25%.

Recent inflation has been running in excess of 3% on an annualized basis and may be accelerating, Waller said, and he fears that business leaders are coming to treat that level as normal and what should be passed through to consumers.

items.excerpt: U.S. businesses’ expectations for inflation over the coming year rose to 2.5% in November, while a separate measure of expected unit costs remained above its prepandemic average. The year-ahead business inflation expectation increased from 2.3% in October, a rise of 0.2 percentage point. The unit-cost measure stayed above its 2.0% prepandemic average. The 2.5% reading is for business inflation expectations; the 2.0% figure is the prepandemic average for unit-cost expectations. The November results were released Wednesday, Nov. 18.

The CMAs, billed as “country music’s biggest night,” celebrate a major milestone with its 60th ceremony, with Lainey Wilson hosting for the third consecutive year from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena. As the entertainment world has done since her passing in August, the CMAs will pay tribute to country legend Dolly Parton, with Kacey Musgraves set to honor her idol. Returning to the CMA stage for the first time in 13 years, Taylor Swift is scheduled to perform her nominated song, “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5. Accepting this year’s Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award: famed duo Brooks & Dunn, with country stars including Luke Bryan, Marcus King, Brothers Osborne, Halestorm, and HARDY participating in their celebration. items.excerpt: Raye and Rosalia lead nominations for music's Grammy Awards British singer Raye, the artist behind the genre-mixing hit that asks "Where Is My Husband!," landed at the top of the list of Grammy Award nominees on Monday, ahead of Spanish musician Rosalia and "Choosin' Texas" artist Ella Langley. Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Rosalia racked up nine nominations, days after she dominated the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux."
